chosen_line.card: All Streams Flow to the Sea

q1_what_did_you_play: Read the Current into Nibbit first, then All Streams Flow to the Sea into Nibbit. That is both energy on the two biggest hits. Read the Current is 7 plus 6 for being at 12 Charge, so 13; All Streams is a printed 11 with the Charge already folded in. 24 damage total, taking Nibbit from 40 to 16. I led with Read the Current specifically because it is the card that cares about the Charge threshold — if anything I played consumed Charge, I wanted the 10-or-more check to happen while I was certainly at 12. All Streams reads as a fixed 11 regardless, so it loses nothing by going second.
q2_other_line_considered: Coral Guard plus All Streams Flow to the Sea: 5 Block and 11 damage. I weighed it and dropped it. Block 5 against a 12-damage telegraph absorbs 5 and lets 7 through, so it buys 5 HP; playing Read the Current instead buys 13 damage. At 48/70 I am not near any threshold that makes 5 HP worth more than 13 damage on a 40-HP enemy I need at least two more turns to chew through. Water's Edge never got in — it is strictly a worse Read the Current at this Charge (6 versus 13 for the same 1 energy), so it was never a candidate for either slot.
q3_what_it_gave_up: All the defence. I eat the full 12 and drop to 36/70, where the Coral Guard line would have left me at 41. I also spent the Charge-fed Read the Current now rather than banking it — if Charge drains and I do not rebuild it above 10, that card is a 7 next time instead of a 13, so I cashed the premium version at the moment it was worth the most. And I end the turn with Coral Guard and Water's Edge still in hand, which may or may not survive to next turn depending on how the hand cycles.
q4_different_intent: Yes, though it takes a fairly specific telegraph. A 12-damage attack is survivable and 5 Block barely dents it, so no ordinary attack number moves me — even a considerably larger attack mostly argues for more damage, not for a 5-Block card that would still let most of it through. What would change the line is a telegraph where 5 Block crosses a real boundary: an attack in the 5-to-7 range that Coral Guard fully or nearly negates, or a multi-hit intent where each small hit gets blunted. A defensive or block-gaining intent on Nibbit would also swing me harder toward damage right now before its Block lands, but that is the line I am already playing. Nothing about this particular 12 changed my mind.
